remaining_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by tenant and does not exclude the affected use case, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate.
The risk acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment, so there is no approved risk acceptance covering the limitation.
The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The governing policy text states that rollback capability, dashboards, or a small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
Public guidance on monitoring and model cards does not override the specific internal policy condition for launch.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is analytically cleaner, but it does not close the policy failure. The admissible evidence still shows: the affected health-plan benefits support segment is below target and exposed in rollout; the rollout is random by tenant and does not exclude that use case; the risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment; and policy requires disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The policy text further states that rollback controls and a small rollout percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. A caveated position can matter when caveats satisfy the governing predicate; here they do not. So this is not compliant_with_caveats. It remains noncompliant on the present record.
